toolsSettings.activateHelp: A tool can be turned on once a dry run has succeeded.
toolsSettings.argumentsHelp: The values the assistant fills in when it calls the tool. Use one in the call below by writing {{args.name}} wherever it belongs.
toolsSettings.builtInRemoveConfirm: Remove the saved Tavily API key? Web search will stop working until a new key is added.
toolsSettings.builtInSearchLimitInvalidToast: Enter a whole number between 1 and 20.
toolsSettings.builtInSearchLimitDescription: Hard limit on how many web searches the AI may run while answering a single message. Lower it to save search credits; raise it for research-heavy use.
toolsSettings.builtInSubtitle: Credentials for tools built into the platform, rather than ones you define yourself.
toolsSettings.builtInWebSearchDescription: Lets assistants search the web for current information. Get a key from tavily.com.
toolsSettings.credentialHelp: Anything written as {{credential.name}} in the call is filled in from here. Values are encrypted, are never shown again, and stay hidden in dry run results.
toolsSettings.credentialNoneHelp: This tool uses no secret values. To add one, write {{credential.api_key}} wherever the secret belongs in the call above — a field for it appears here.
toolsSettings.credentialValuesRequiredToast: Enter a value for each secret before saving.
toolsSettings.deleteConfirm: Delete the tool "{{name}}"? Assistants using it will stop being able to call it.
toolsSettings.descriptionHelp: The assistant reads this to decide when to use the tool. Be specific about what it does and when it is the right choice.
toolsSettings.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. Create an issue in our tracker and return its identifier.
toolsSettings.dryRunErrorTitle: The dry run could not be made
toolsSettings.dryRunHelp: Makes one real call with the test values. A tool stays a draft until a dry run succeeds.
toolsSettings.errorArgumentDuplicate: Two arguments share a name. Each one needs its own.
toolsSettings.errorArgumentName: Argument names use letters, numbers and underscores, and start with a letter.
toolsSettings.errorArgumentUnknown: The call uses {{name}}, which is not one of the arguments above.
toolsSettings.errorDescriptionLength: The description needs to be between {{min}} and {{max}} characters.
toolsSettings.errorMaxChars: Choose a limit between 1 and {{max}} characters.
toolsSettings.errorNameFormat: Use 3 to 64 characters: lowercase letters, numbers and underscores, starting with a letter.
toolsSettings.errorNameReserved: “{{name}}” is already the name of a built-in tool. Pick another.
toolsSettings.errorPathRequired: Enter the path to the value you want.
toolsSettings.errorTooManyArguments: A tool can take at most {{max}} arguments.
toolsSettings.errorUrlHttps: The address has to start with https://.
toolsSettings.errorUrlOrigin: The address up to the first / is fixed — arguments can only be used from the path onwards.
toolsSettings.maxCharsHelp: Longer responses are cut off at this length before the assistant sees them.
toolsSettings.nameHelp: This is the name the assistant calls. Lowercase letters, numbers and underscores.
toolsSettings.outboundMissing: The server did not report the request it sent.
toolsSettings.rawResponseTitle: 2. The response, as it came back
toolsSettings.rawTruncated: Cut off at the character limit above.
toolsSettings.subtitle: Let your assistants call your own APIs. Describe a tool once — what it does, what it takes, and which call to make — then dry run it before you turn it on.
toolsSettings.testValuesHelp: The values a dry run calls with. They are only used for the test.
toolsSettings.testValuesNone: This tool takes no arguments, so a dry run needs no test values.
toolsSettings.title: Tools
toolsSettings.transformMode_json: The whole response, as formatted JSON
toolsSettings.transformPathHelp: A dotted path, such as data.issue.identifier. Use a number to pick an item from a list, such as items.0.title.
toolsSettings.urlHelp: Has to start with https://. The address up to the first / is fixed; from the path onwards you can use {{args.name}}.

connectorsSettings.approvalLabelHelp: Only you see this. It is what names the connection in the list above.
connectorsSettings.approvalLead_one: {{server}} offers 1 tool. If you approve, your assistants are told about it: they see the name and description below, and may call it.
connectorsSettings.approvalLead_other: {{server}} offers {{count}} tools. If you approve, your assistants are told about every one of them: they see the names and descriptions below, and may call any of them.
connectorsSettings.approvalNothingYet: Nothing has been added yet, and nothing is added unless you approve it.
connectorsSettings.approvalPinned: The list is saved exactly as you approve it here. If the server starts offering different tools later, your assistants keep to this list — the new one has to be approved on this page before they are told about it.
connectorsSettings.approvalTitle: Approve what your assistants will be told about
connectorsSettings.chooseMcpHelp: Give us the address, then approve the tools the server offers.
connectorsSettings.chooseSpec: An API you have the description for
connectorsSettings.chooseSpecHelp: Give us the address of its OpenAPI or Swagger description, then pick the operations you want as tools.
connectorsSettings.credentialNameHelp: The name the key is stored under. Anything else that uses the same key can share it.
connectorsSettings.disconnectConfirm_one: Disconnect "{{label}}"? This deletes the one tool it added, and assistants using it will stop being able to call it.
connectorsSettings.disconnectConfirm_other: Disconnect "{{label}}"? This deletes all {{count}} tools it added, and assistants using them will stop being able to call them.
connectorsSettings.discoverErrorTitle: The server could not be asked
connectorsSettings.discoverErrorToast: Error asking the server what it offers.
connectorsSettings.errorUrlHttps: The address has to start with https://.
connectorsSettings.importedHelp: They arrive as drafts. Each one has to pass its own dry run on the Tools page before it can be turned on.
connectorsSettings.mcpKeyHelp: The key we identify ourselves to the server with. It is encrypted and stored before the server is asked anything, and never travels in a request that describes this connector.
connectorsSettings.previewErrorTitle: The description could not be read
connectorsSettings.selectionFull: That is as many as one import can bring in. Untick one to pick another.
connectorsSettings.selectionHelp: Pick up to {{max}}. Every tool you bring in is described to your assistants on every request, so a long list costs you on each one and makes the choice harder for them.
connectorsSettings.serverUrlHelp: Paste the address of the server. We ask it what tools it offers and show you the list — nothing is added until you approve it.
connectorsSettings.skippedTitle_one: 1 operation could not be brought in
connectorsSettings.skippedTitle_other: {{count}} operations could not be brought in
connectorsSettings.specKeyHelp: The key the operations are called with. It is encrypted when it is stored, is never shown again, and never travels in a request that describes this connector.
connectorsSettings.specUrlHelp: Paste the link to the API's OpenAPI or Swagger description. We read it and show you what it offers — nothing is created until you say so.
connectorsSettings.subtitle: Connect something once and get a set of tools from it. You always see what it offers, and decide what your assistants are told about, before anything is added.
connectorsSettings.title: Connectors
